_comment_family: Syne ships as a family - an Extra, a Bold, a Semi Bold and a Regular
- and every one of those files carries 'Syne' as name ID 1, with the
cut in the subfamily. Asking for 'Syne' alone would let any of them
answer, and this face is used as a HIGHLIGHT: a Regular answering in
its place would put a picked word in the same weight as a hand it is
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, the same way
gilroy-extrabold and the two Telegraf packs declare theirs. This file
spells it with a space and its PostScript name with a hyphen, and
both spellings are listed in `local` below rather than one of them
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. Asking for 800 here would invite a browser to synthesise a
weight on top of a face that already has its own.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than the family, so a machine answering to
either is answering with this file - which is exactly what the
fallback route is for. 'Syne' on its own is deliberately absent: it
is the family, and every other weight of it answers to that.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, and the one thing it must not do is fall through
to the same face the block does. This face is a highlight: its whole
job is to be a visibly different hand from Brittany Signature on the
same line, and a stack that ended up at the same substitute would
leave a picked word identical to the words either side of it - a
failure that draws no attention to itself, which is the kind this app
has been bitten by before (see the note in marydale-bold.json).
That is why the two stacks are written as opposites and converge
nowhere: brittany-signature falls through Segoe Script and Brush
Script into `cursive`, and this one falls through Segoe UI and Arial
into `sans-serif`. Whatever a machine is missing, the picked word
stays the grotesque and the block stays the hand.
Impact and Arial Black are absent on purpose. Syne Bold is a display
grotesque, so they are at least the right genus - but they are far
heavier and much narrower than it is, and a highlight substituted by
something louder than the real one is a highlight that has changed
what the caption emphasises rather than merely how.
